title: How AI-Powered Solutions are Transforming Enterprise Software
excerpt: Discover how OpenAI and machine learning integrations are enabling businesses to automate workflows, enhance decision-making, and deliver personalized experiences at scale.
author: ARSTEG Tech Team

content.text: Artificial Intelligence is no longer a futuristic concept - it's reshaping how enterprises build and deploy software today. From intelligent document processing to predictive analytics, AI-powered solutions are delivering measurable business value across industries.
The Rise of AI in Enterprise Software

A large and growing share of enterprises are adopting AI in their software. The integration of large language models has opened new possibilities for automation, customer service, and decision support systems.
Key Applications We're Building

items: Intelligent Document Processing - Extracting and categorizing data from unstructured documents, with a human-review step for low-confidence cases
Conversational AI - Customer service bots that handle complex queries and integrate with backend systems
Predictive Analytics - ML models that forecast trends, detect anomalies, and optimize operations
Content Generation - Automated report writing, email drafting, and personalized communications

content.text: Implementation Best Practices

Success with AI requires more than just integrating APIs. We've found that the most successful implementations focus on clear use cases, quality data preparation, and robust error handling. Start small, measure impact, and scale what works.

In our own work, well-scoped AI automation has let clients take significant manual effort out of document-heavy processes and speed up response times — provided the workflow includes validation and a human-review step.

title: Building Scalable APIs: Patterns That Hold Up in Production
excerpt: An in-depth look at API architecture patterns, authentication strategies, and performance optimizations we've learned from integrating with a wide range of third-party services.
author: Integration Experts

content.text: After integrating with a wide range of third-party APIs - from health devices to payment gateways - we've learned what separates robust integrations from fragile ones. Here are the patterns and practices that have proven most valuable.
Design for Failure

Every external API will fail eventually. Networks go down, rate limits get hit, and providers push breaking changes. The key is building resilience from day one: circuit breakers, retry logic with exponential backoff, and graceful degradation.
Authentication Patterns That Scale

items: OAuth 2.0 for user-authorized access with proper token refresh handling
API keys with rotation strategies and secure storage
JWT tokens with appropriate expiration and revocation capabilities
Webhook signatures for secure event notifications

content.text: Performance Optimization

Caching, connection pooling, and request batching can dramatically improve performance. We've seen 10x improvements in throughput by implementing intelligent caching strategies and reducing redundant API calls.
Monitoring and Observability

You can't fix what you can't see. Comprehensive logging, metrics collection, and alerting are essential. Track latency percentiles, error rates, and upstream availability to catch issues before they impact users.

title: From Legacy to Cloud: Modernizing Without a Big-Bang Rewrite
excerpt: Why the strangler-fig approach is a safer way to modernize an ageing platform than a risky full rewrite — and how we apply it.
author: Development Team

content.text: Ageing platforms tend to struggle in the same ways: slow performance, expensive maintenance, and an inability to ship new features. Here's the approach we use to modernize them without disrupting the business that depends on them.
The Challenge

A typical case: the system is built on classic ASP and VB6 - technology that's increasingly difficult to maintain. Finding developers is nearly impossible, and every change carries risk. The business needs to modernize but can't afford downtime.
Our Approach: Strangler Fig Pattern

Instead of a risky big-bang rewrite, we used the strangler fig pattern. We built new microservices in .NET Core that gradually replaced legacy functionality. Both systems ran in parallel, with traffic gradually shifted to the new platform.
What good looks like

items: No downtime during the migration itself
A modern codebase that developers actually want to work on
Deployments that move from occasional to on-demand

content.text: Lessons Learned

The biggest lesson: don't try to modernize everything at once. Start with high-value, low-risk components. Build confidence and momentum before tackling the core systems. And always maintain the ability to roll back.
